Research method

Compare architecture.
Then compare products.

“Semantic layer” now describes several different control points. The Atlas keeps them in one directory while making the differences explicit.

M—01

The taxonomy

Six patterns,
six jobs.

A product may span more than one pattern. Its primary category reflects the architectural job it performs best—not its marketing label.

01

Standard

Portable metadata contracts. They describe meaning but do not necessarily execute queries.

Example · Apache Ossie
02

Semantic layer

Independent query runtimes serving multiple consumers through APIs or standard protocols.

Examples · Cube, dbt, AtScale
03

Warehouse-native

Semantic objects governed and executed inside the data platform.

Examples · Snowflake, Databricks
04

BI-native

Rich models optimized for a primary analytics experience.

Examples · LookML, Power BI, Omni
05

AI analytics

Conversational consumers grounded by curated models and business context.

Examples · Genie, Spotter
06

Open-source BI

BI frontends with local semantics or adapters to external semantic runtimes.

Examples · Superset, Metabase

What each profile covers

Evidence, fit, and friction.

01

Identity & market age

What the product actually is, who owns it, deployment shape, license posture, maturity, and an approximate time in market.

02

Semantic scope

Metrics, measures, dimensions, entities, joins, hierarchies, security, time semantics, AI context, and other supported objects.

03

Operating model

How teams author, validate, deploy, query, govern, and consume the model.

04

Pros, cons & best fit

Editorial synthesis of trade-offs. These are design signals, not vendor rankings.

05

Primary sources

Official documentation, project sites, and first-party release history. Vendor claims are identified as such through source context.

M—03

Editorial scoring

A compass,
not a leaderboard.

ExpressivenessDepth of model, calculations, relationships, and dimensional behavior.

InteroperabilityBreadth of consumers, protocols, export paths, and model portability.

GovernanceAccess control, lifecycle, versioning, auditability, and controlled reuse.

AI readinessAgent context, governed query paths, natural-language consumption, and evaluation.

OpennessOpen source, open specifications, accessible APIs, and avoidance of proprietary boundaries.

Scores compress nuance. A lower score can be a better architectural fit: a thin open-source BI layer may be exactly right when a dedicated runtime already owns semantics.
